newsitem.title: CANADA: Edper, Hees win investor favor.
newsitem.headline: Edper, Hees win investor favor.

text.p: Buyers again flocked to Hees International Bancorp Inc and Edper Group Ltd stock on Monday, lured by high yields and real estate's return to favor.

One trader cited speculation that complicated negotiations dealing with the World Financial Center in lower Manhattan, formerly owned by Olympia & York's U.S. unit, would soon conclude with the Bronfman group in clear control.
Hees and Edper are holding companies atop the Bronfman group of companies, with direct or indirect stakes in such companies as Brascan Ltd and Noranda Inc.
Hees president Robert Harding said the World Financial Center negotiations were before the courts and declined to elaborate.

Harding said the Bronfman group already controlled three of the four World Financial Center towers, but that the negotiations were designed to transfer that interest to an equity stake in a company that would own the buildings.

The two companies inked a merger deal in October that is due to close in December, subject to shareholder approval. The union is designed to simplify the complicated corporate structure of the Bronfman group.
Since the merger was announced, investors have grabbed up the shares -- as well as Edper receipts -- in heavy volume.
"I think the stock prices have been moving up nicely since the announcement of the amalgamation," Harding said in a telephone interview.
He said there were no other corporate developments to account for the moves.

Edper shares rose 0.45 to 7.10, a new 52-week high, on the Toronto Stock Exchange on 751,762 shares. The Edper receipts spiked 7.50 higher to 78.50, just off a 52-week peak of 80 hit earlier in the session. Volume topped 4.2 million shares.
Hees rose 1.30 to 19.35, just shy of the 19.40 year high set earlier, on turnover of 1.39 million shares.
-- Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com
